_why: The window each clip is read at in the runner's nightly (the EP's decision of 2026-11-14: a runner cannot read a whole clip, so each clip is read as a window at its worst moment, collapse at 60 ticks; the full reading stays a local run on Orb's PC). skip is run-pixels.mjs's --skip (ticks run without a picture first; the window starts at tick skip + 1). A clip with no entry is read from tick 1 for defaultTicks, the speed trial's way. 'from' says how the moment was found: an entry that has not been measured says so. tools/flash/nightly-windows.mjs --check reads this file.

collapse-normal.from: not measured: collapse costs about 21 s a tick on a runner (run 43575965534), so 60 ticks from tick 1 until a full local reading names its worst second

clash-normal.from: ticks 951 to 1120 (170): the full local reading of clash-normal (960x540, hardware, 2026-11-14, HEAD 97df40b8 export) has its worst second at ticks 1075 to 1113; the window read the same nine ticks (one off by a tick) and the same primary 4.5; 124 ticks of lead-in give the two-second memory its history

clash-reduced.from: as clash-normal (same scene and seed; the reduced mode and the night sky are assumed to peak at the same moment: not measured)

clash-night-normal.from: as clash-normal (same scene and seed; the reduced mode and the night sky are assumed to peak at the same moment: not measured)

clash-night-reduced.from: as clash-normal (same scene and seed; the reduced mode and the night sky are assumed to peak at the same moment: not measured)
